I've been to a psychiatrist twice in my life. The first was when I was around 14. I just discovered the internet and figured I'd give one of those online personality tests a shot. It said I was severely depressed and I showed the results to my parents. It was the wake up call they needed to see that I was fucked up. They sent me to therapy but unfortunately it didn't help. They kept changing psychologists on me so I never built up rapport or trust, so I never spoke openly. They also put me on antidepressants that didn't work.

I went again a few years ago in my early 20s. This time it was much better. I was older so I didn't care about building a rapport but I did really like the psychologist anyway. It was also cognitive behavioural therapy, which is the good kind. We focused on fixing what was wrong rather than talking about it. With her help I even published a book. She also didn't put me on any pills and encouraged me to solve my problems with actions, rather than pills. I made a lot of progress with her.

Long story short is that therapy can help. As long as you get the right kind and a good therapist. If you're worried about your behaviour then go for CBT. If you just want someone to talk to you want counselling.

Remember, the psychiatrist does not want to cure you. In fact, he is financially incentivized to get you into as many sessions as he can. As soon as you stop taking the drugs or coming to the sessions, they stop getting paid. Psychiatric medications are poorly understood, and the studies that determine their efficacy are inherently flawed due to the nature of self reporting as well as what constitutes an affirmative result. In a psychiatric drug study, the efficacy of the drug is determined on whether it induces a change in the mental state of the patient. People with extreme depression are excluded from studies of depression medications.

The anti-psychotic drugs are equally poorly understood. I suppose if you were looking for some Adderall or some such drug you'd be okay since the stimulants are actually way better researched. I'd steer right the fuck away from antidepressants or antipsychotics, those drugs will seriously fuck you up in both short and long term. The other problem with drugs like that is that you have to take them for weeks before your brain equilibrates to their presence, which means that when you decide that you want to feel your emotions again, you have weeks where you feel EVEN WORSE. Just google antidepressant tapering if you want to see how bad it fucks people up.
